edit_summary.reason: The main engine reward is too easy to obtain (any distance decrease gives +2). The hovering penalty (-0.5) is too weak to discourage non-descending engine use. We need to make the main engine reward conditional on both distance decreasing AND vertical descent (vy < 0), but we must avoid the failed pattern from iter_003 where the main engine reward was conditional only on vy<0 (which caused the agent to stop using the main engine). By keeping the distance-decreasing condition AND adding a vy<0 condition, the agent must both move toward the pad AND descend to get the reward. This prevents the agent from collecting reward by moving sideways or upward. Additionally, we increase the hovering penalty to -2.0 (from -0.5) to strongly discourage hovering without descent. We also increase the success bonus to +300 to make landing more attractive relative to per-step rewards. The descent reward scale is increased to 1.0 to provide stronger shaping for reducing vertical speed.

edit_summary.reason: Restructure the main engine reward to be a one-time bonus of +10 when the agent first descends below a distance threshold (distance < 0.5), instead of a per-step reward. This prevents the agent from collecting large rewards by slowly descending from high altitude. Increase the hovering penalty from -0.5 to -1.5 per step when |vy|<0.1 and distance is not decreasing, to make hovering more costly. Add a small progress bonus of +0.1 * (prev_distance - distance) when distance is decreasing, to provide continuous feedback for descending. Keep the success bonus at +200, crash penalty at -100, progress shaping at -1*distance -0.3*|vy|, fuel costs at -0.03*m_power -0.02*s_power, angle penalty at -0.05*|angle|, and descent reward at 0.5*(prev_vy - vy) when m_power>0 and vy<0. The expected behavior is that the agent will descend to the pad to collect the one-time main engine bonus and the success bonus, while the increased hovering penalty will discourage hovering.
